A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLMC research, with matching authors, title, problem and principal convergence bounds. All 22 pages of v3 and 26 pages of v4, including their appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports theoretical convergence bounds and mathematical proofs, including its appendices. Its comparison table contains theoretical complexities, not original empirical results.

after.justification: v4 remains entirely theoretical. Its added algorithms and gradient-moment lemma do not report experiments, simulations or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Both versions study the same overdamped and underdamped PLMC samplers using Bernoulli midpoint corrections. v4 reformulates notation and documents efficient implementations without establishing a new sampler or algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical test scenarios. Both analyze strongly log-concave sampling through overdamped and underdamped Langevin dynamics.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. The same theoretical LMC, RLMC and earlier PLMC comparisons appear in v3 Table 1 and v4 Tables 1–2.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental evaluation protocols. Changes to theorem conditions and theoretical step-size requirements belong to T1.

E4.justification: Neither PDF contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies or case studies. The added discussion of moment bounds is theoretical interpretation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Expectations and concentration bounds occur within mathematical analysis.

E6.justification: The corresponding complexity tables retain the same bounds and comparator entries. Neither version reports empirical scores; the additional parameter specializations in v4 restate consequences of existing complexity expressions.

T1.justification: v4 adds Lemma 12 and its integration-by-parts proof for higher stationary gradient moments. It changes the underdamped theorem from a transformed joint-state bound to a position-marginal statement, changes the stated friction constant threshold from 2 to sqrt(2), and adds an explicit small-epsilon restriction to Corollary 2. Most proofs and headline complexity exponents remain.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged. Both versions claim cubic accuracy improvements over Euler–Maruyama, improved randomized-midpoint bounds, and Wasserstein convergence complexity below strong-L2 error lower bounds. v4 emphasizes the implications without changing these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 identifies unfavorable dimension and condition-number dependence generally. v4 adds a specific explanation: Remark 8 attributes potentially improvable condition-number dependence to loose gradient and momentum moment bounds. Section 4 also argues that the overdamped gradient-sum bound is tight at stationarity.

D1.justification: v3 refers to prior work for efficient implementation. v4 adds Algorithms 1–2 specifying midpoint selection, Gaussian accumulation, corrections and batch updates, alongside explicit arithmetic-complexity discussion. This substantially expands local implementation documentation, although Algorithm 1's batch scaling conflicts with the retained recurrence.

R1.justification: All 32 references are retained. v4 expands the comparison with Altschuler et al. [2] by translating its KL guarantee into a Wasserstein guarantee and discussing parameter tradeoffs. It also newly characterizes epsilon^(-2/3) Wasserstein optimality as widely believed or conjectured.

P1.justification: v4 substantially rewrites the introduction, sampler explanation and proof overview, changes notation throughout, moves contributions into Section 1.1, and relocates v3 Sections 5–6 into appendices C and F. The appendix organization and concluding discussion are also extensively reworked.

P2.justification: The small, side-by-side comparisons in v3 Table 1 become two larger, separate tables in v4, with clearer complexity headings. Two algorithm displays are added. These are substantive but localized display changes; no experimental figures are introduced.

improvement.justification: v4 provides clearer organization, more readable tables, a supporting lemma and additional implementation detail. However, new Algorithm 1 uses eta/k for full-batch drift and correction terms where the retained recurrence and Appendix D.3 require eta. This undermines the implementation guidance. The explanatory gains and this concrete technical defect leave the net quality direction uncertain.
